````markdown
# Identity runbook — V2 foundation M03

> **Current platform scope — 2026-10-15:** Build and deploy the Windows version only. Linux is allowed only as an optional VM guest for qualified isolation; standalone Linux hosts/releases are deferred. This supersedes earlier platform assumptions in this document. PostgreSQL/Redis and ordinary integration/security tests remain in the Windows work queue. Preserve required protections and tests; unsupported executable paths stay disabled. See ADR 0004.

`@asi/identity` is a trusted library for issuing, verifying, reducing and revoking authorization. The qualification image imports the library; it does not supply an HTTP service. Keep signing configuration and the PostgreSQL connection in the trusted governance process. Workers receive bounded tokens and public Principal claims, never keys, database handles or provider credentials.

## Durable bootstrap

1. Apply reviewed prerequisite `db/postgres/migrations/001-control.sql`, then forward migration `009-identity-grants.sql` through the trusted schema owner. Never edit an applied 001. Production migration journaling/runner qualification belongs to M04; M03 applies this closure only to a disposable qualification schema.
2. Create the tenant through the existing trusted owner. Configure a dedicated identity runtime role with schema USAGE and SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE on `identity_grants`. Give it no schema ownership, DDL, TRUNCATE, worker-accessible connection or superuser privileges. The trigger denies physical DELETE and prevents claim mutation, clearing revocation and reversing deletion. Workers receive no table privileges.
3. Obtain signing keys and a connected PostgreSQL client through trusted bootstrap. The injected client exposes parameterized `query(text, values)`; the service owner bounds connection/query timeouts and cancellation. The existing qualified control pg driver satisfies this interface; identity adds no driver dependency.
4. Call `configureIdentity({ keys: trustedKeys, defaultKid: trustedDefaultKid })` and `setGrantStore(new PostgresGrantStore(trustedDatabaseClient))` before serving authorization. Import these functions/classes from `@asi/identity`.

These are trusted bootstrap values, never task fields. The library implements no environment reader. A service may resolve `IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEYS_JSON` privately; adding it to the worker environment is rejected by the qualification profile. Missing configuration, unknown grants and database failure deny authorization. There is no automatic memory fallback. Unit tests explicitly choose `createMemoryGrantStore()`.

## Issuance and verification

Only the trusted policy/governance owner calls `createPrincipalToken(principal)` after its own authorization checks. This port is not an untrusted request handler. Issuance validates the Principal, bounds expiry by the signing key and persists immutable authority before returning the token. Failed writes return no token. An interrupted response may leave an unused grant; M03 does not claim exactly-once issuance.

`verifyPrincipal(token, expectedAudience)` validates JWT header/payload schemas, HS256 signature, issuer `asi-identity`, audience, current key validity and token times. A live canonical grant must match tenant, subject, roles, optional agentId, capabilities, audience, issuance, expiry and parent. Returned roles/agentId preserve the authenticated identity.

Grant issuance/expiry and JWT times use integer Unix **seconds**. Key creation/expiry and revocation use Unix **milliseconds**. Consumers verify at each authorization point; a cached Principal is not permanent permission.

## Delegation and revocation

Call `delegatePrincipal(parent, capabilities, audience, expiresAt)` with the original object returned by verification, or the unchanged original object successfully passed to trusted issuance in the same process/store context. Constructed, serialized, cloned or edited Principals have no delegation authority. After reconnect or restart, verify the parent token again to establish a new binding.

The child keeps its parent's tenant, receives a capability subset and cannot outlive its parent. Persistent parentGrantId connects the chain. Verification walks at most **16 ancestor links** and denies unknown, expired, future, revoked, cyclic, over-depth or widened ancestry. Descendants cannot regain permission after parent revocation.

`revokeGrant(grantId, reason)` returns false for unknown IDs, true for an existing or successful new revocation, and throws on store failure. First revocation time/reason survive concurrent updates. `isGrantRevoked` checks only the record's own revocation and throws for unknown IDs; use `verifyPrincipal` for effective authorization including ancestors.

`GrantStore.delete` creates a durable tombstone so delayed writes cannot resurrect the ID. Administrative retention/purge policy needs separate reviewed governance and is not implemented here. Runtime roles cannot physically delete. Revocation is observed at subsequent authorization checks, including new processes; it does not retroactively cancel an already-authorized external effect. Effect cancellation belongs to its owning task.

## Migration and key rotation

Historical memory tokens and records missing canonical identity claims require authenticated reissuance. Never backfill authority from an untrusted token. Original task 03 evidence and Principal wire contracts are preserved; M03 tracks V2 readiness separately.

Generate keys with `generateSigningKey(kid, ttlMs)` in trusted bootstrap. IDs must be unique, defaultKid must exist, and expiry must follow creation. Add a new key while retaining valid old keys, distribute configuration, then change defaultKid. Remove old keys after their authorization window, or immediately on compromise alongside trusted grant revocation. Future/expired key checks apply to signing and verification. Never log key configuration or tokens.

## Local qualification and limits

`infra/Dockerfile.identity` pins official Node 24.19.0 by digest, copies explicit manifests and compiled contracts/identity artifacts, installs their production dependency closure plus the existing control pg driver with a frozen lockfile and disabled lifecycle scripts, and runs as non-root. Compile both packages before building `asi/identity:m03-qualification`.

`infra/compose.yaml` has an explicit `qualification` profile. Its worker has no private mounts or credential configuration, a read-only root, user 1000, network none, all capabilities dropped and no-new-privileges. Tests inspect the actual process and deny synthetic credential injection without printing values.

Run the named checks from the root:

```powershell
pnpm exec vitest run --project unit packages/identity/test/grants.test.ts
pnpm exec vitest run --project security tests/security/credentials.test.ts
pnpm typecheck
pnpm exec vitest run --project integration tests/integration/identity-v2-restart.test.ts
```

The current credential tests use native Windows identity processes with sanitized environments and explicit private bootstrap. OS-level credential/filesystem isolation still requires Task12 qualification; removed image/mount checks are historical and are not claimed passed by these tests. Integration uses local PostgreSQL on Windows with a disposable `*_qualification` database, unique schema and restricted role, applies 001/009, and removes its own schema/role. Default local endpoint is port 60636/database `asi_m03_qualification`; `M03_TEST_DATABASE_URL` overrides it privately. Never target production.

Independent native identity processes on Windows verify PostgreSQL-backed authority across process restart. Synthetic trusted bootstrap goes through private stdin, never worker mounts, task payloads or printed logs. The trusted qualification runner may create disposable schemas; bootstrap privileges do not define the runtime role.

Evidence separates unit, real PostgreSQL, native identity restart and historical Linux process/mount receipts. Linux deployment files are removed from the active product. The Windows release host must repeat its host-specific checks; repeat guest-specific checks only if the optional VM is used. Standalone Linux release-host qualification is deferred. M03 does not qualify the full Gateway service, Task 12 sandbox, production migration runner or deployment.

## Operations

Use bounded trusted health probes for key validity, database connectivity and expected-audience verification without exposing configuration. Route safe summaries and IDs to the owning audit system; this library has no audit sink. Deny dependent effects on failure, then investigate clock skew, audience, keys, canonical claims, ancestry, tombstones or database availability. Do not broaden permissions or switch to a fixture store to recover service.


````

````markdown
# Observability Runbook

> **Current platform scope — 2026-10-15:** Build and deploy the Windows version only. Linux is allowed only as an optional VM guest for qualified isolation; standalone Linux hosts/releases are deferred. This supersedes earlier platform assumptions in this document. PostgreSQL/Redis and ordinary integration/security tests remain in the Windows work queue. Preserve required protections and tests; unsupported executable paths stay disabled. See ADR 0004.

> Qualification notice (2026-10-10): this is the Task10 operational reference. Consult [the consolidated guide](../v2-build-guide.md#start-here) and live task qualification before using these procedures. Example endpoints, commands, alerts and deployment snippets require matching implementation and service acceptance; this document does not certify them.


## Overview

The ASI Agent System provides comprehensive observability through three pillars:

1. **Distributed Tracing** - OpenTelemetry-based spans for runs, tasks, and effects
2. **Metrics** - Prometheus-compatible metrics for system health and performance
3. **Structured Logging** - Redacted, correlated logs with privacy-first design

## Architecture

```
┌─────────────────┐     ┌──────────────────┐     ┌─────────────────┐
│   Application   │────▶│  Telemetry SDK   │────▶│  OTLP Exporter  │
│   (spans,       │     │  (spans,         │     │  (OTLP/HTTP)    │
│   metrics,      │     │   redaction,     │     └────────┬────────┘
│   redaction)    │     │   metrics)       │              │
└─────────────────┘     └──────────────────┘              │
                                                         ▼
                                                ┌─────────────────┐
                                                │  Backend        │
                                                │  (Jaeger,       │
                                                │   Prometheus,   │
                                                │   Grafana)      │
                                                └─────────────────┘
```

## Components

### 1. Spans (`@asi/telemetry`)

#### Starting a Run Span

```typescript
import { startRunSpan, TraceHandle } from "@asi/telemetry";
import type { RunContext } from "@asi/contracts";

const handle: TraceHandle = startRunSpan({
  runId: "run-123",
  sessionId: "session-456",
  writerEpoch: 1,
  mode: "execute",
  deadlineAt: new Date(Date.now() + 3600000).toISOString(),
  budgetRef: {
    tenantId: "tenant-1",
    accountId: "account-1",
    rootRunId: "run-123",
  },
});

// Use the handle
handle.addEvent("task.started", { taskId: "task-1" });
handle.setAttribute("custom.key", "value");

// End the span
handle.end("ok");
```

#### Recording Usage and Quality

```typescript
import { recordUsage, recordQuality } from "@asi/telemetry";
import type { RunContext } from "@asi/contracts";

recordUsage(runContext, 1000, 50000); // 1000 tokens, $0.05
recordQuality(runContext, "eval-123", 0.95);
```

#### Task and Effect Spans

```typescript
import { startTaskSpan, startEffectSpan } from "@asi/telemetry";

const taskHandle = startTaskSpan(runContext, "task-123", "research");
taskHandle.end("ok");

const effectHandle = startEffectSpan(runContext, "effect-456", "model.invoke", "model:gpt-4");
effectHandle.end("ok");
```

### 2. Redaction (`@asi/telemetry`)

#### Automatic PII/Secret Redaction

```typescript
import { redactString, redactSpanAttributes, configureRedaction } from "@asi/telemetry";

const input = "Contact john@example.com with API key sk-1234567890";
const redacted = redactString(input);
// Result: "Contact [EMAIL] with API key [API_KEY]"

// Redact span attributes automatically
redactSpanAttributes(attributes);
// { "user.email": "user@example.com", "api.key": "sk-secret" }
// → { "user.email": "[EMAIL]", "api.key": "[API_KEY]" }
```

#### Custom Redaction Rules

```typescript
import { configureRedaction } from "@asi/telemetry";

configureRedaction({
  enabled: true,
  customRules: [
    { pattern: /INTERNAL_ID_\d+/g, replacement: "[INTERNAL_ID]" },
    { pattern: /CUSTOM_TOKEN_[A-Z0-9]+/g, replacement: "[CUSTOM_TOKEN]" },
  });
}
```

#### Disabling Redaction (Testing)

```typescript
configureRedaction({ enabled: false });
// Redaction disabled - useful for testing
```

### 3. Metrics (`@asi/telemetry`)

#### Run Metrics

```typescript
import { recordRunStart, recordRunEnd, recordUsage } from "@asi/telemetry";

recordRunStart("tenant-1");
// ... run execution ...
recordRunEnd("tenant-1", 5000, true); // 5s duration, success
recordUsage(runContext, 1000, 50000); // tokens, cost in micro-USD
```

#### Tool and Memory Metrics

```typescript

## Troubleshooting

### Exporter Connection Issues

```bash
# Check endpoint connectivity
curl -v http://localhost:4318/v1/traces

# Verify environment variables
env | grep OTEL
```

### Missing Spans

1. Check `telemetryEnabled` flag
2. Verify tracer registration
3. Check span processor configuration
4. Verify exporter endpoint

### Missing Metrics

1. Check `metricsEnabled` flag
2. Verify meter provider registration
3. Check metric reader configuration
4. Verify OTLP metrics endpoint

### Redaction Not Working

1. Verify `configureRedaction({ enabled: true })`
2. Check custom rules syntax
3. Verify span attribute processing

## Runbook: Exporter Failure

### Symptoms
- Spans/metrics not appearing in backend
- Exporter logs show connection errors

### Diagnosis
1. Check exporter endpoint reachability
2. Verify authentication/headers
3. Check network policies/firewall

### Recovery
1. Restart telemetry SDK (re-register exporter)
2. Fallback to local file export
3. Alert on-call engineer

### Post-Incident
1. Verify data integrity
2. Backfill missing spans/metrics if possible
3. Update runbook with lessons learned

## Security Considerations

- All telemetry data is redacted before export
- API keys, PII, secrets automatically redacted
- Custom redaction rules for organization-specific patterns
- Redaction cannot be disabled in production (enforced by CI)
- Exporter credentials rotated quarterly
- Network policies restrict exporter egress
````

````markdown
# Recovery Runbook

> **Current platform scope — 2026-10-15:** Build and deploy the Windows version only. Linux is allowed only as an optional VM guest for qualified isolation; standalone Linux hosts/releases are deferred. This supersedes earlier platform assumptions in this document. PostgreSQL/Redis and ordinary integration/security tests remain in the Windows work queue. Preserve required protections and tests; unsupported executable paths stay disabled. See ADR 0004.

> Qualification notice (2026-10-10): this is the Task19 operational reference. Consult [the consolidated guide](../v2-build-guide.md#start-here) and live task qualification before using these procedures. Example endpoints, commands, alerts and deployment snippets require matching implementation and service acceptance; this document does not certify them.


## Overview

This runbook covers the recovery procedures for the ASI agent system, including run recovery, approval management, circuit breaker handling, and fault injection testing.

## Architecture Overview

The recovery system consists of:

1. **Run Recovery** (`packages/orchestrator/src/recover.ts`) - Recovers interrupted runs from checkpoints
2. **Retry Logic** (`packages/orchestrator/src/retry.ts`) - Jittered exponential backoff with error classification
3. **Circuit Breakers** (`packages/orchestrator/src/circuit-breaker.ts`) - Per-dependency circuit breakers
4. **Approval Management** (`packages/gateway/src/approvals.ts`) - Human-in-the-loop approval workflows

## Recovery Procedures

### 1. Run Recovery

#### Automatic Recovery
The system automatically attempts to recover runs that:
- Are in `running`, `awaiting_tool`, `awaiting_approval`, or `awaiting_model` status
- Have not been updated for more than 5 minutes
- Have a valid checkpoint (not older than 24 hours)

#### Manual Recovery
If automatic recovery fails:

```bash
# List runs needing recovery
psql -d asi_test -c "SELECT run_id, status, updated_at FROM run_state WHERE status IN ('running', 'awaiting_tool', 'awaiting_approval', 'awaiting_model') AND updated_at < NOW() - INTERVAL '5 minutes';"

# Manually trigger recovery for a specific run
# (Requires API call to /runs/:runId/recover endpoint)
```

#### Recovery Failure Handling
If a run cannot be recovered:
1. Run is marked with status `reconciliation_pending`
2. Reason is recorded in `reconciliation_reason` field
3. Alert is sent to on-call operator
4. Manual intervention required

### 2. Circuit Breaker Management

#### Viewing Circuit Breaker Status
```bash
# View all circuit breakers
curl -X GET http://localhost:8080/circuit-breakers/stats

# View specific dependency
curl -X GET http://localhost:8080/circuit-breakers/stats/<dependency-id>
```

#### Manual Circuit Breaker Operations

**Force Open (Emergency Stop):**
```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/circuit-breakers/<dependency-id>/force-open
```

**Reset to Closed:**
```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/circuit-breakers/<dependency-id>/reset
```

**View Metrics:**
```bash
curl -X GET http://localhost:8080/circuit-breakers/stats
```

#### Circuit Breaker Configuration
Default thresholds:
- Failure threshold: 5 consecutive failures
- Success threshold (half-open): 2 successes
- Timeout: 30 seconds
- Half-open max requests: 3

To modify:
```bash
curl -X PUT http://localhost:8080/circuit-breakers/<dependency-id>/config \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"failureThreshold": 10, "timeoutMs": 60000}'
```

### 3. Approval Management

#### Viewing Pending Approvals
```bash
# List all pending approvals
curl -X GET http://localhost:8080/approvals/pending

# For specific run
curl -X GET http://localhost:8080/approvals/pending?runId=<run-id>
```

#### Approving/Denying
```bash
# Approve
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/approvals/<approval-id>/approve \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"principal": {...}, "reason": "Approved by operator"}'

# Deny
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/approvals/<approval-id>/deny \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"principal": {...}, "reason": "Security policy violation"}'
```

#### Cleanup Expired Approvals
```bash
# Manual cleanup (runs automatically every hour)
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/approvals/cleanup
```

### 4. Fault Injection Testing

The system includes a fault injection framework for testing recovery:

```bash
# Run fault injection tests
npm run test:fault-injection

# Specific fault scenarios:
npm run test:fault-injection -- --scenario=provider-429
npm run test:fault-injection -- --scenario=postgres-failure
npm run test:fault-injection -- --scenario=redis-partition
npm run test:fault-injection -- --scenario=sqlite-disk-full
npm run test:fault-injection -- --scenario=kill-before-checkpoint
npm run test:fault-injection -- --scenario=kill-after-checkpoint
npm run test:fault-injection -- --scenario=expired-approval
npm run test:fault-injection -- --scenario=provider-429-retry
```

#### Test Scenarios

| Scenario | Description | Expected Outcome |
|----------|-------------|------------------|
| `provider-429` | Provider returns 429 rate limit | Circuit breaker opens, retries with backoff |
| `postgres-failure` | PostgreSQL connection fails | Circuit breaker opens, run marked for reconciliation |
| `redis-partition` | Redis network partition | Circuit breaker opens, cached data served |
| `sqlite-disk-full` | SQLite disk full error | Run fails, marked for reconciliation |
| `kill-before-checkpoint` | Process killed before checkpoint | Run cannot recover, marked for reconciliation |
| `kill-after-checkpoint` | Process killed after checkpoint | Run recovers from checkpoint |
| `expired-approval` | Approval expires before decision | Run marked failed, notification sent |
| `provider-429-retry` | Provider 429 with retry | Jittered backoff, eventual success |

### 5. Recovery Commands

#### Operator Commands

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `recover-runs` | Trigger automatic recovery of interrupted runs |
| `recover-run <run-id>` | Manually recover specific run |
| `reconcile-run <run-id>` | Manually reconcile run |
| `circuit-breaker status <dep-id>` | View circuit breaker status |
| `circuit-breaker reset <dep-id>` | Reset circuit breaker to closed |
| `circuit-breaker force-open <dep-id>` | Force circuit breaker open |
| `approval list` | List pending approvals |
| `approval approve <id> --reason "..."` | Approve a pending approval |
| `approval deny <id> --reason "..."` | Deny a pending approval |
| `recovery replay <run-id>` | Replay run from checkpoint |
| `recovery reconcile <run-id>` | Manually reconcile run |

#### Example Usage

```bash
# Recover all interrupted runs
npx tsx packages/orchestrator/src/recover.ts --limit 50

# Recover specific run
npx tsx packages/orchestrator/src/recover.ts --run-id run-abc123

# Check circuit breaker status
npx tsx packages/orchestrator/src/circuit-breaker.ts --status

# List pending approvals
npx tsx packages/gateway/src/approvals.ts --list-pending
```

## Monitoring and Alerts

### Key Metrics to Monitor

| Metric | Warning Threshold | Critical Threshold |
|--------|------------------|-------------------|
| Run recovery rate | < 90% | < 70% |
| Circuit breaker open rate | > 10% | > 30% |
| Pending approvals age | > 1 hour | > 4 hours |
| Recovery time | > 5 min | > 15 min |
| Reconciliation queue | > 10 | > 50 |

### Alerting Rules

```yaml
# Prometheus alerts (example)
- alert: HighRecoveryFailureRate
  expr: rate(recovery_failures_total[5m]) / rate(recovery_attempts_total[5m]) > 0.3
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: critical
  annotations:
    summary: "High recovery failure rate"

- alert: CircuitBreakerOpen
  expr: circuit_breaker_state{state="open"} == 1
  for: 2m
  labels:
    severity: warning
  annotations:
    summary: "Circuit breaker {{ $labels.dependency }} is open"

- alert: PendingApprovalsAging
  expr: time() - approvals_requested_at_timestamp > 3600
  for: 1h
  labels:
    severity: warning
  annotations:
    summary: "Pending approval older than 1 hour"
```

## Recovery Scenarios Reference

### Scenario 1: Provider Returns 429 (Rate Limited)

1. **Detection**: Tool call returns 429 status
2. **Classification**: `RATE_LIMITED` error → `retry` decision
3. **Backoff**: Exponential backoff with jitter (1s, 2s, 4s, 8s, 16s, max 30s)
4. **Circuit Breaker**: Failure count increments, may trip after 5 failures
5. **Retry**: Up to 3 attempts with exponential backoff
6. **Recovery**: On success, circuit breaker resets; on continued failure, circuit opens

### Scenario 2: PostgreSQL Failure

1. **Detection**: Database connection/query fails
2. **Classification**: `DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE` → `retry`
3. **Circuit Breaker**: Trips after 5 failures
4. **Run State**: Run marked `awaiting_recovery`
5. **Recovery**: After DB recovers, run resumes from checkpoint
6. **Reconciliation**: If no checkpoint, run goes to `reconciliation_pending`

### Scenario 3: Redis Partition

1. **Detection**: Redis connection timeout
2. **Classification**: `DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE` → `retry`
3. **Circuit Breaker**: Opens after 5 failures
4. **Graceful Degradation**: Serve stale cache data if available
5. **Recovery**: Auto-recovers when Redis available

### Scenario 4: SQLite Disk Full

1. **Detection**: SQLite returns `SQLITE_FULL`
2. **Classification**: `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` → `fail`
3. **Run State**: Marked `failed`
4. **Alert**: Critical alert to operator
5. **Resolution**: Manual cleanup required, then run replay

### Scenario 5: Process Killed Before Checkpoint

1. **Detection**: Run stuck in `running` status > 5 minutes
2. **Checkpoint Check**: No valid checkpoint found
3. **Action**: Mark `reconciliation_pending` with reason "No checkpoint available"
4. **Operator Action**: Manual review required

### Scenario 6: Process Killed After Checkpoint

1. **Detection**: Run stuck in `running` status > 5 minutes
2. **Checkpoint Check**: Valid checkpoint found (< 24 hours old)
3. **Recovery**: Reconstruct state from checkpoint
4. **Resume**: Continue execution from checkpoint
5. **Verification**: Compare output hash with expected

### Scenario 7: Expired Approval

1. **Detection**: Approval `expires_at` < `NOW()` and status = `pending`
2. **Action**: Auto-update status to `expired`
5. **Run Impact**: Parent run marked `failed` with reason "Approval expired"
6. **Notification**: Alert sent to requestor

### Scenario 8: Provider 429 with Retry

1. **Detection**: Tool call returns 429
2. **Classification**: `RATE_LIMITED` → `retry`
3. **Backoff**: 1s, 2s, 4s, 8s, 16s, 30s (max)
6. **Circuit Breaker**: Tracks failures per provider
7. **Recovery**: On success, breaker resets; continues execution

## Escalation Procedures

### Level 1: Automated Recovery
- Automatic retry with backoff
- Circuit breaker management
- Checkpoint-based run recovery

### Level 2: Operator Intervention
- Manual approval/denial
- Circuit breaker reset
- Manual run recovery
- Approval expiry handling

### Level 3: Engineering Escalation
- Database corruption
- Persistent circuit breaker trips
- Data inconsistency detected
- Security incident

## Contact Information

- **Primary On-Call**: #asi-oncall Slack channel
- **Escalation**: #asi-escalation Slack channel
- **Documentation**: Confluence space "ASI Operations"
- **Runbooks**: This document + individual component runbooks

## Revision History

| Version | Date | Author | Changes |
|---------|------|--------|---------|
| 1.0 | 2026-10-09 | System | Initial version |
````

````markdown
> **V2 consolidation (2026-10-07):** Read [the unified V2 build guide](../../v2-build-guide.md) for the combined target, completed-task migrations and extension task cards. This file remains a source record; its historical status prose is not current completion evidence. New V2 boundaries await recorded review.

> **Current platform scope — 2026-10-15:** Build and deploy the Windows version only. Linux is allowed only as an optional VM guest for qualified isolation; standalone Linux hosts/releases are deferred. This supersedes earlier platform assumptions in this document. PostgreSQL/Redis and ordinary integration/security tests remain in the Windows work queue. Preserve required protections and tests; unsupported executable paths stay disabled. See ADR 0004.

# Agent Workspace Frontend — Step-by-Step Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:executing-plans for native execution or superpowers:subagent-driven-development if the human authorizes task agents. Read both specs and the machine baselines before editing. Complete checkbox steps task-by-task; this file authorizes no implementation by itself.

**Goal:** Build all seven frontend sections with a usable streaming chat, inline questions/approvals, reviewed UI components, and integration with the existing protected Gateway architecture.

**Architecture:** The web app belongs to Client Surfaces and sends every command through the Gateway. One application-owned conversation reducer and one GatewayClient power the UI; backend identity, policy, privacy routing, memory and tool execution retain authority. Start with a simulated Gateway using the same wire contracts, then integrate real read APIs and the protected run flow.

**Tech Stack:** Proposed Next.js App Router, React 19, TypeScript 5.9.x strict, Tailwind CSS 4, shadcn/ui, AI Elements presentation, Zod 4.6.5 contracts, Vitest/Testing Library/Playwright. Exact compatible versions and component-source digests are frozen in U01. User-listed alternative libraries are reviewed through one component inventory.

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-06-agent-workspace-ui-design.md`.
**System spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-06-asi-agent-design.md`.
**System plan:** `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-06-asi-agent-build.md` (existing tasks 01–30).
**UI tracking:** `docs/ui-baseline.json`, `docs/ui-task-ledger.json`.
**Status:** PROPOSED. Product code, UI libraries and application tests have not been installed or implemented in this planning request.

## Global constraints

- Exactly seven primary sections with labels/routes/order fixed in UI spec section 3.
- Clarifications, approvals and their canonical decision controls render inside Chat.
- A management-screen approval navigates to its backend-owned conversation; Activity links rather than duplicates decision controls.
- Clarification answers never grant effect permissions; question and approval contracts/actions remain separate.
- One conversation state owner, one GatewayClient, one selected primary chat presentation stack.
- All frontend operations traverse the Gateway; no provider/DB/tool/sandbox execution path in browser or Next inference route.
- Backend is authoritative for decisions, permission, effective model, trust, outcomes and usage.
- Mock/live modes are explicit and never automatically substitute for each other.
- Vendor components are qualified/pinned/wrapped; all source/license/dependency choices are recorded.
- Existing system R01–R24 and all 12 pictured component IDs remain preserved.

## Review focus

1. A reconnect/duplicate delta or late event from an old conversation must not duplicate text or overwrite another chat. Tests: U03/U05/U19/U21.
2. An approval click, expired proposal, double tab or stale version must not silently authorize or display completed execution. Tests: U09/U19/U21.
3. A yes/no question response must not dispatch an approval command. Tests: U08/U09/U21.
4. Provider keys, private memory, attachments and preview content must not leak through browser persistence/rendering or wrong workspace state. Tests: U06/U10/U11/U14/U17/U21.
5. Multiple component libraries/agents must not introduce duplicate navigation, global approval pages, competing stores, hidden provider routes or incompatible themes. Tests: U01/U04/U09/U20/U21.

## 1. The unambiguous build order

1. U01–U02: freeze stack and shared UI contracts. Reuse existing system workspace/contracts tasks 01–02; do not scaffold a second unrelated repository.
2. U03: implement a simulated Gateway with contract tests and reproducible scenarios. This is the minimal backend foundation needed to build the UI.
3. U04–U10: build shell and complete Chat interaction flow.
4. U11–U16: implement the other six sections and their links into Chat.
5. U20: validate responsive/accessibility behavior while the real backend is being prepared.
6. U17–U18: connect authenticated real Gateway and progressively available catalog/configuration APIs.
7. U19: connect real protected model/tool/question/approval flow only after existing system tasks 01–16 and recovery task 19 pass.
8. U21–U22: perform conformance/security/recovery tests and release/handoff.

You do not need to finish the full agent backend before starting U04. A demo frontend is complete at the demo gate after U16/U20; real-system completion requires U17–U19/U21/U22. These are separate completion claims.

The UI tasks do not replace existing system tasks. Web integration adds browser-safe Gateway projections and another Client Surface. CLI/Slack remain optional delivery adapters for later milestones; policy/privacy/isolation gates are unchanged.

## 2. Fixed navigation and component placement

| Order | Label | Route | Canonical components owned here |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Chat | `/chat`, `/chat/:conversationId` | ConversationRail, Composer, messages, ClarificationCard, ApprovalCard, TaskProgressCard, ToolActivityCard, ArtifactCard |
| 2 | Models & Providers | `/models` | ProviderList, ProviderConnectionForm, ModelCatalog, default/preference controls |
| 3 | Skills | `/skills` | SkillLibrary, SkillDetails, trust/availability/permission display |
| 4 | Tools & Connections | `/connections` | ToolCatalog, MCP/A2A/messaging connection lists and forms |
| 5 | Memory | `/memory` | Authorized memory search, detail, sources/revisions, correction/deletion request |
| 6 | Activity & Tasks | `/activity` | Cross-chat run/task summary, usage, safe error/evidence and “Open conversation” |
| 7 | Settings | `/settings` | Profile, appearance, privacy, budgets, schedules, retention settings |

`/approvals`, `/questions`, `/agents` and `/dashboard` are not primary routes in this plan. Decision badges/links navigate to `/chat/:conversationId?interaction=:interactionId`. A tab/drawer inside a section is not a new primary navigation entry. All pages reuse the same AppShell and common state/contracts.

## 3. File map and one-owner boundaries

```text
apps/web/
  package.json, next.config.ts, tsconfig.json, components.json
  src/app/layout.tsx, globals.css
  src/app/(workspace)/layout.tsx
  src/app/(workspace)/chat/page.tsx
  src/app/(workspace)/chat/[conversationId]/page.tsx
  src/app/(workspace)/models/page.tsx
  src/app/(workspace)/skills/page.tsx
  src/app/(workspace)/connections/page.tsx
  src/app/(workspace)/memory/page.tsx
  src/app/(workspace)/activity/page.tsx
  src/app/(workspace)/settings/page.tsx
  src/features/shell/{AppShell,AppSidebar,ConversationRail}.tsx
  src/features/chat/{ChatPage,ConversationPanel,MessageRenderer,Composer}.tsx
  src/features/chat/cards/{ClarificationCard,ApprovalCard,TaskProgressCard,
                          ToolActivityCard,ArtifactCard}.tsx
  src/features/{models,skills,connections,memory,activity,settings}/
  src/lib/gateway/{client,http-client,sse,errors}.ts
  src/lib/chat/{store,reducer,selectors,intents}.ts
  src/lib/auth/{session,csrf}.ts
  src/lib/content/{markdown,artifact-policy}.ts
  src/lib/navigation.ts
  src/test/{fixtures,harness}/
packages/ui/src/{tokens.css,vendor/,adapters/,components/}
packages/contracts/src/ui/{conversation,events,interactions,commands,catalogs,index}.ts
apps/gateway-fixture/src/{main,scenarios,fixtures}.ts
apps/gateway/src/ui/{routes,auth,stream,projections,commands,uploads}.ts
tests/ui/{contracts,navigation,chat,clarification,approval,catalogs,state}/
tests/ui/{e2e,security,accessibility,visual}/
scripts/{verify-ui-boundaries,verify-ui-sources}.mjs
docs/ui-component-inventory.json
docs/ui-baseline.json
docs/ui-task-ledger.json
docs/release-evidence/frontend.md
```

No new `apps/web` provider-generation route is added. Next rewrites/ingress proxy only forward `/api/ui/v1` to the Gateway. API DTOs are authored in shared contracts, not separately invented in pages. Page owners cannot edit navigation labels, approval authority, event schema/store, vendor imports or system protected files without the shared-contract owner and reviewed change.

## 4. Public interfaces executors must use

Wire schemas/fields are specified in UI spec sections 5–7. U02 exports the following types. All mutation results are UiCommandResult; expectedVersion/expectedRevision are server revisions, not arbitrary client timestamps.

```ts
interface GatewayClient {
  getMe(): Promise<WorkspaceSession>;
  listConversations(cursor?: string): Promise<Page<ConversationSummary>>;
  createConversation(commandId: string): Promise<ConversationSummary>;
  updateConversation(id: string, input: ConversationPatch): Promise<UiCommandResult>;
  getSnapshot(id: string): Promise<ConversationSnapshot>;
  sendMessage(id: string, input: SendMessageInput): Promise<UiCommandResult>;
  subscribe(id: string, after: number, signal: AbortSignal): AsyncIterable<UiEvent>;
  cancelRun(runId: string, commandId: string): Promise<UiCommandResult>;
  answerClarification(id: string, input: ClarificationAnswer): Promise<UiCommandResult>;
  decideApproval(id: string, input: ApprovalDecisionInput): Promise<UiCommandResult>;
  beginUpload(input: UploadIntent): Promise<UploadView>;
  uploadContent(id: string, file: File, signal: AbortSignal): Promise<void>;
  completeUpload(id: string, commandId: string): Promise<UploadView>;
  getModels(): Promise<Catalog<ModelView>>;
  getProviders(): Promise<Catalog<ProviderView>>;
  getSkills(): Promise<Catalog<SkillView>>;
  getConnections(): Promise<Catalog<ConnectionView>>;
  queryMemory(input: MemorySearchInput): Promise<Page<MemoryView>>;
  getActivity(input: ActivityQuery): Promise<Page<TaskView>>;
  getSettings(): Promise<SettingsView>;
  submitCommand(command: UiMutationCommand): Promise<UiCommandResult>;
}

function reduceConversation(state: ConversationState, event: UiEvent): ConversationState;
function hydrateConversation(snapshot: ConversationSnapshot): ConversationState;
function navigateToInteraction(conversationId: string, interactionId: string): string;
```

Supporting exact shapes to define in U02:

- `Page<T>`: items, nextCursor (string|null). `Catalog<T>`: items, revision, availability (ready/unavailable/permission_denied), safe reason when unavailable.
- `WorkspaceSession`: workspaceId, displayName, subjectId, allowedActions, demoMode, csrfToken, limits (maxMessageBytes/maxAttachmentBytes/maxAttachmentCount); no provider secrets. Client does not set authoritative tenant/role.
- `SendMessageInput`: clientMessageId, commandId, text, attachmentIds, requestedModelId?, requestedSkillIds, expectedConversationRevision.
- `ConversationPatch`: commandId, expectedRevision, title? or archived?; a strict union ensures the intended change is explicit.
- `ClarificationAnswer`: commandId, expectedVersion, optionIds, text?; backend validates per-question cardinality/free-text rule.
- `ApprovalDecisionInput`: commandId, expectedVersion, decision (approve/reject); effect/input binding comes from server-owned proposal. A client cannot submit replacement action arguments.
- `UploadIntent`: commandId, fileName, mimeType, byteSize; `UploadView`: uploadId, attachmentId?, status (pending/uploading/scanning/ready/rejected), safe reason. Actual digest/status checked by backend.
- `MemorySearchInput`: query, authorized requested scope?, cursor?, limit (1–100). `ActivityQuery`: status?, conversationId?, cursor?, limit (1–100).
- `UiMutationCommand`: discriminated union of provider.connect/disconnect, model.preference.set, skill.install/enable/disable/revoke, connection.connect/disconnect, memory.correct/delete, settings.update; each includes commandId, expectedRevision, target IDs and its schema-validated payload. Permission-sensitive settings are server commands; local theme is separate.
- Provider credential submission is a write-only field restricted to provider.connect. Schema redaction excludes it from UiCommandResult/events/transcripts/snapshots. After submission the UI clears the field even if a resulting approval remains pending. Gateway stages credentials in the approved backend credential vault/privacy service and places only an opaque credential reference in ordinary command records/outboxes; rejected/expired requests clean up staged credentials. No plaintext key is persisted in an audit/episode/task payload.
- `ConversationState`: conversationId, workspaceId, revision, lastEventSequence, messages, interactions, tasks, tools, artifacts, runStatus, effectiveModel, usage. Local draft/scroll/submitting maps are separate and never serialized as server truth.

Event sequence and revisions are nonnegative safe integers. Payload type names and variants must match the UI spec. Core backend `suspended` + `suspendReason: user_input` maps to UI “Waiting for your answer”; no new core run state is invented by a component.

## 5. Commands and per-task completion cycle

U01 adds `pnpm ui:typecheck`, `pnpm ui:build`, `pnpm ui:test`, `pnpm ui:test:e2e`, `pnpm ui:test:security`, `pnpm ui:test:a11y`, `pnpm ui:verify:boundaries`, `pnpm ui:verify:sources`, `pnpm ui:verify`.

Named test command: `pnpm exec vitest run tests/ui/<file>.test.ts` (use .tsx for rendered component tests). Browser checks use `pnpm exec playwright test tests/ui/e2e/<file>.spec.ts`. ui:verify combines typecheck/build/unit/boundary/source checks; release adds e2e/security/a11y/visual checks. Missing live backend is a failed live gate, never a silent mock pass.

For each task: read deps/spec → add the named behavior tests → run and observe meaningful RED → implement only owned files/interfaces → run GREEN plus affected checks → review → update UI ledger evidence → commit after Git setup. Exact assertions below become executable tests with fixtures authored in that task; fixture values are not new public APIs.
````

````markdown
> **V2 consolidation (2026-10-07):** Read [the unified V2 build guide](../../v2-build-guide.md) for the combined target, completed-task migrations and extension task cards. Linux is allowed only as an optional VM guest for qualified isolation; standalone Linux hosts/releases are deferred. This supersedes earlier platform assumptions in this document. PostgreSQL/Redis and ordinary integration/security tests remain in the Windows work queue. Preserve required protections and tests; unsupported executable paths stay disabled. See ADR 0004.

# ASI TypeScript Agent System Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox syntax for tracking. Execution method has not been selected; this request authorizes planning only.

**Goal:** Build the pictured TypeScript agent architecture in verifiable increments, with enforced component boundaries and reviewable changes.

**Architecture:** Preserve the 12 pictured components, use Mastra inside a deterministic shell, and keep policy, provider credentials, memory credentials, and executable tools behind distinct trusted boundaries. Start on one Windows host with the requested web Chat surface, one specialist, SQLite episodes, PostgreSQL curated memory/control state, and BullMQ/Redis. Add breadth and experimental learning only after the protected vertical slice passes.

**Tech Stack:** Proposed Node 24 LTS, TypeScript 5.9.x strict ESM, Zod 4.6.5, Mastra 1.x, Hono, AI SDK, PostgreSQL 17/pgvector, SQLite FTS5/WAL, BullMQ/Redis, OpenTelemetry/Langfuse, qualified Windows-hosted isolation (optional Linux VM guest), MCP and A2A.

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-06-asi-agent-design.md` (PROPOSED; read it with this plan).

**Frontend guide:** `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-06-agent-workspace-ui-build.md` supplies U01–U22 and the precise seven-section/inline-approval UI design. Start its shared contracts and simulated Gateway after this plan's workspace/contracts tasks 01–02; build the UI while backend work continues. Real UI integration waits for its named backend gates. This extension prioritizes web Chat within Client Surfaces and preserves backend task IDs/architecture. A simulation is not a completed protected slice.

## Global constraints

- Preserve all 12 component IDs and the pictured primary flow; document refinements with traceability.
- Policy, approval logic, signing keys, and architecture protection cannot be modified by runtime agents or evolved candidates.
- All model calls, including embeddings, summarizers, judges, and background jobs, traverse the privacy router.
- Workers obtain reduced scoped identities; supervisor credentials never travel in task payloads.
- Executable tool handlers run in qualified isolation; unknown/untrusted/generated handlers require the qualified microVM backend.
- Memory “Global” means tenant-global. Role and Private add narrower scope; cross-tenant retrieval is forbidden for text and vectors.
- Start compression consideration at 0.50; force it at 0.85 before another inference call. Preserve stable prefix and complete tool-call/result groups.
- Every effect has a durable intent and a signed final/unknown-outcome receipt; never assert global exactly-once effects.
- No architecture/dependency substitution without a written decision and explicit human review of the change.
- Exact dependency versions and image digests are resolved in Task 01 before product scaffolding; failed compatibility qualification blocks dependent work.
- No source is implemented in this planning turn. All tasks below are pending. Proposed assumptions and review decisions are in spec sections 1 and 14.

## Review focus

1. Duplicate or out-of-order events and crashes after a remote effect: preserve durable input and avoid blind duplicate execution. Tasks 04, 13, 16, 19, 25.
2. Stale writer/revoked identity racing takeover: prevent late episode, effect, memory, and reply commits. Tasks 03, 07, 08, 09, 16, 19.
3. Retrieval or consolidation leaking tenant/private data: scope text, vectors, embeddings, summaries, and publication. Tasks 09, 11, 17, 26.
4. Background/child work overspending or exceeding context: share atomic reservations, bound recursion/output, preserve prefix and tool groups. Tasks 06, 14, 15, 17, 21, 26, 29.
5. Malicious skill/tool/remote result or protocol change: verify artifact provenance, enforce the runtime boundary, validate versions, and protect promotion gates. Tasks 12, 13, 18, 22, 23, 27, 29, 30.

## 1. Execution rules

Use the approved spec/baseline as the source of architecture decisions. Read root AGENTS.md before each task. Only start a task when its dependencies and phase gate are satisfied. Assign an implementer explicit task ID, requirement IDs, file set, interfaces, and acceptance tests; do not give an agent “build the platform” as an unbounded instruction.

For each implementation task:

- [ ] Read its consumed interfaces and the relevant spec sections; identify baseline differences before editing.
- [ ] Add the named behavior tests and fixtures; run the task command and observe a meaningful failure. Missing tooling/setup alone is not the behavior failure.
- [ ] Implement the listed boundary and required values; keep unrelated files untouched.
- [ ] Run the task command to pass, then affected integration/architecture checks. Do not substitute a passing unit test for a security integration test.
- [ ] Review requirements, changed files, credential/egress implications, and evidence. Record test counts/output and remaining limitations.
- [ ] Update `docs/task-ledger.json`; commit the reviewed task with a focused message after Git setup exists. A task can have smaller commits; completion requires all acceptance evidence.

Tests below include exact assertions for the important behavior. Fixture names in examples describe test harness results, not new product APIs; each task creates its own fixtures alongside the named test. Public interfaces listed below are the stable product boundary; HTTP/queue adapters validate the same schemas.

No automatic subagent dispatch is authorized by the mere presence of this plan. Choose native or subagent execution with the user before implementation. Where multiple agents are later used, contract tasks complete before their consumers, and overlapping files have one owner. Security/evolution tasks require a reviewer distinct from the implementer.

## 2. Proposed file structure

```text

          telemetry,privacy,models,sandbox,tools,specialists,

          consolidation,evolution,observations}/src/

         verify-protected-files,verify-traceability,verify-all}.mjs

App files are composition roots; business logic lives in the owning package. Direct cross-app imports are forbidden. Contracts/ports cross the boundary; application credentials and schema/session adapters do not.

## 3. Commands and evidence convention

Task 01 creates these actual workspace scripts: `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm build`, `pnpm test:unit`, `pnpm test:integration`, `pnpm test:security`, `pnpm test:protocols`, `pnpm test:e2e`, `pnpm test:load`, `pnpm verify:architecture`, `pnpm verify:dependencies`, `pnpm verify:traceability`, and `pnpm verify`.

Use Vitest for named test files: `pnpm exec vitest run <path>`. Unit tests use deterministic fake models. Integration/security/protocol tests use actual PostgreSQL runtime roles and real Windows-hosted isolation where applicable; a Linux guest is allowed only inside an optional VM. Database-only tests do not require Linux or KVM. Test service startup/teardown is owned by a test harness and cannot silently fall back to mocks when integration dependencies are missing. `pnpm verify` executes lint, typecheck, build, unit, architecture, dependency, and traceability checks; full release validation adds integration/security/protocol/e2e/load suites.

Targeted run before implementation: named assertions FAIL. Run after implementation: all named assertions PASS, no skips, exit 0. Security gates fail if infrastructure is absent. Record platform/kernel/backend/version with results. Real model evals are separately budgeted; fake model tests establish control correctness, not model quality.

- [ ] Commit/handoff only with approved integration method. Do not mark the entire roadmap complete while optional/unsupported features remain unlabeled.

## 11. Small details that are release requirements

These are owned by the task IDs shown and must be in their fixtures/runbooks rather than left to agent improvisation.

| Detail | Rule | Task |
|---|---|---|
| IDs and time | Opaque IDs; UTC wire timestamps/deadlines; tenant timezone only for schedules/display | 02, 21 |
| Monetary math | Integer micro-USD; no floating-point quota comparisons | 02, 06 |
| Input limits | 1 MiB JSON; attachment references with size/MIME/provenance, no unbounded inline blobs | 02, 16, 20, 24 |
| Tool output | 64 KiB inline; artifact references beyond that; exact output schema and normalized error | 13 |
| Interactive limits | 120-second run, 30-second default tool, 12 model iterations, depth 2, fanout 8, retry attempts 3 for known retryable failures | 06, 13–16, 19 |
| Lease timing | 30-second lease; renew every 10 seconds using server time; monotonically increasing epoch | 04, 08, 15 |
| Restart boundaries | Crash tests around each durable append/effect/delivery/commit boundary; unresolved effects retained | 04, 08, 13, 19, 25 |
| SQL roles | Migration owner separate from runtime; FORCE RLS; no runtime superuser/BYPASSRLS; broker authenticates scope | 09 |
| Vector retrieval | Tenant/scope filter in actual query; dimensions/provider version recorded; no client-side post-filter-only protection | 09, 11 |
| Local-only data | Failure to run approved local model denies cloud fallback; redaction ambiguity stays restricted | 11 |
| DNS/egress | Reject metadata/private/redirect targets unless approved; authorization binds destination and method | 07, 12, 22, 23 |
| Manifest lifecycle | Digest/signature/revocation checked at install and execution; do not execute while discovering | 13, 18, 27 |
| Approvals | Authenticated approver; exact input/artifact/policy hash; expiration/single use; status visible | 07, 19 |
| Memory revision | Version CAS; provenance/source IDs; no audience widening; contradictory facts preserve evidence | 09, 26, 28 |
| Cache correctness | Stable prefix byte hash; token accounting plus provider overhead; no orphan tool groups | 17 |
| Trace privacy | Payload collection opt-in/reviewed; exports redact sensitive keys; telemetry is not audit authority | 05, 10 |
| Cancellation | Abort provider/queue/handler, terminate child processes, revoke stale authority, deny late publication | 12–16, 19 |
| Shutdown | Stop acceptance, drain bounded work, persist remaining state, release/expire leases safely | 19, 25 |
| Backup | PostgreSQL consistent backup plus SQLite backup API/WAL-consistent snapshot; timed clean restore | 08, 25 |
| Keys/secrets | Separate scoped service secrets, key IDs/rotation/revocation; no secrets in source/log/eval snapshots | 03, 05, 25 |
| Data deletion | Explicit approved retention settings; remove derived source projections; minimal non-content receipt | 25 |
| Upgrade | Exact version/digest inventory, schema/protocol compatibility fixtures, reversible rollout | 01, 02, 22, 23, 25 |
| Eval independence | Held-out tests outside candidate write scope; predeclared criteria; model judges treated as fallible evidence | 10, 26, 29 |
| CI honesty | Missing security infrastructure fails gate; no critical skips, fake pass, or disabling protections | 01, 30 |

## 12. Completion and next decision

Planning is complete when the spec and this plan can be reviewed together, every pictured component/requirement maps to tasks, dependencies are acyclic, links exist, and all unresolved product/deployment choices are explicit.

Implementation begins only after review of the proposed spec/plan and selection of execution method. Recommended execution: first run Tasks 01–16 sequentially with distinct review for security boundaries; authorize independent task agents later only where completed contracts and disjoint files make that safe. The next concrete build action is Task 01, not scaffolding the entire roadmap or jumping to DGM.

No implementation tests have been run in this planning task because application/test code does not yet exist. Document validation is reported separately from future system validation.
````

````markdown
# Agent Workspace Frontend — Proposed Design and Agent Boundary Rules

Date: 2026-10-06. Status: PROPOSED; documentation only.

Build guide: `../plans/2026-10-06-agent-workspace-ui-build.md`.
System architecture: `2026-10-06-asi-agent-design.md`.
UI baseline: `../../ui-baseline.json`. Task ledger: `../../ui-task-ledger.json`.

## 1. Purpose and relationship to the existing plan

The original 30-task plan covers the agent system and its backend/security build. It does not supply a complete screen-by-screen web frontend sequence. This spec and the companion guide supply that missing sequence, including sidebar, chat, interactive questions/approvals, all seven sections, shared contracts, a mock Gateway, and real-backend integration gates.

The latest user request prioritizes a web frontend and names eleven UI component sources. The web app is another Client Surface (`channels`) connected to the same Unified Gateway. None of the 12 architecture components is removed or bypassed. CLI/Slack remain adapters that can be delivered later; the web app does not become the orchestrator or policy service.

Build order: minimal reproducible workspace + shared contracts → simulated Gateway → frontend → authenticated real Gateway/read APIs → protected real run flow → full validation. A simulated UI may be built before the real agent backend is complete. Real external actions remain disabled until their existing system gates pass.

Working library assumption: AI Elements is the primary chat presentation layer; shadcn/ui is the shared shell/control foundation; application-owned typed state and one GatewayClient own interactions. Other user-listed libraries are a component-source catalog with reviewed, explicit roles. A question about primary-library preference was sent to the user; absence of an answer is not approval. The guide remains a proposed default and can be revised without implementing product code.

## 2. Library selection and compatibility decisions

| Source | Verified information / inspection status | Proposed role |
|---|---|---|
| [21st.dev AI blocks](https://21st.dev/community/libraries/s/ai) | Catalog of multiple AI component collections | Discover selected suggestions/loaders/empty-state blocks; review each item's source, license, dependencies |
| [AI Elements](https://elements.ai-sdk.dev/) | shadcn-based AI components; Conversation, Message, Prompt Input, Confirmation, Tool, Model Selector and other components are documented | Primary chat presentation; copied source wrapped by project components |
| [assistant-ui](https://www.assistant-ui.com/docs/runtimes/custom/external-store) | ExternalStoreRuntime can adapt an application's existing chat state | Supported alternative if selected; one adapter preserves the project store and contracts. Do not run a second independent conversation store |
| [AI/UI](https://ui.kitn.ai/) | Framework-agnostic web components; React/custom-element integration requires its own adapter | Optional artifact/voice surface after React event/property/theme qualification; no second whole-chat widget |
| [AgentUI](https://www.agentui.pro/) | React agent components include approval, activity, usage and model-selection surfaces | Candidate source for project QuestionCard/ApprovalCard/activity styles; source and props qualified before adoption |
| [Rendyn](https://rendyn.dev/) | React source catalog and component previews are accessible | Candidate approval/progress/command-palette blocks; development-time catalog access only |
| [VLLNT UI](https://ui.vllnt.com/docs) | Documentation describes registry/source installation; homepage fetch failed in this tool context | Optional progress/status blocks; verify current source exports and peer/theme compatibility before inclusion |
| [ai2.design](https://ai2.design/) | shadcn-compatible registry and semantic variants documented | Optional form/confirmation styling; map into the common token/primitive system |
| [Smartera UI](https://smarteraui.com/) | React/registry source and token/accessibility system documented | Candidate settings/forms/tables; avoid importing a second global token system without mapping |
| [Control UI](https://control-ui.dev/get-started) | Source registry with chat/workspace patterns; site labels itself alpha | Candidate thread rail/task/context layouts; install individual qualified blocks, freeze source |
| [Codesweep UI](https://codesweep.ai/ui/CATALOG.html) | Supplied catalog URL could not be retrieved; no official source/API/license was established during this inspection | Pending source qualification; agents must not invent exports or claim it was installed/verified |

All eleven sources are represented in the selection inventory. This does not mean eleven complete design systems are installed simultaneously. Assign one provider to each project component slot. If the user requires components from every source, qualify them one at a time; inaccessible/incompatible items remain explicitly pending instead of silently substituted.

Exact versions, registry item URLs, source hashes, licenses, peer dependencies, source-derived transitive dependencies, and wrapper ownership are recorded in UI Task U01. Do not copy a website's component count, “production-ready” claim, CDN snippet, model-calling route, or installer instructions as architecture requirements.

Proposed frontend stack: Next.js App Router, React 19, TypeScript 5.9.x strict, Tailwind CSS 4, shadcn/ui with one qualified primitive variant, AI Elements presentation. AI Elements' [setup page](https://elements.ai-sdk.dev/docs/setup) currently lists React 19, Tailwind 4, an AI SDK setup, and Next.js prerequisites; qualify exact compatible releases rather than guessing package versions. Existing Node 24 baseline applies. AI SDK UI types/rendering may be used; provider SDK credentials and generation routes remain in the backend privacy service.

All vendor imports/source live behind `packages/ui/src/vendor/` and `packages/ui/src/adapters/`; feature code imports project wrappers. A source registry/MCP server used to obtain UI code is a development tool and is unrelated to the product's runtime MCP integrations screen.

## 3. Exactly seven primary navigation sections

The sidebar is part of the shared workspace shell. The active section renders in the main panel. Seven section entries appear in the default authenticated workspace, in this order:

| ID | Exact label | Route | Screen contents | Interaction destination |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `chat` | Chat | `/chat`, `/chat/:conversationId` | Conversation rail, messages, composer, contextual model/skill selectors, questions, approvals, progress, results | Current conversation |
| `models` | Models & Providers | `/models` | Connected providers, authorized models, local/cloud status, effective/default model preferences, masked connection state | Policy-gated changes link to their conversation approval |
| `skills` | Skills | `/skills` | Installed versions, description, verification/availability, required permissions, enable/install/revoke requests | Selection in composer; installation/permission approval in Chat |
| `connections` | Tools & Connections | `/connections` | Tools, MCP servers, A2A remote agents, messaging connections, status, granted permissions | Connection/effect approval in Chat |
| `memory` | Memory | `/memory` | Authorized saved facts, sources, scopes, revision history, search, correction/deletion request | Policy-gated mutation approval in Chat |
| `activity` | Activity & Tasks | `/activity` | Runs, specialist/task progress, safe tool summaries, errors, tokens/cost, receipt references | “Open conversation” navigates to owning question/approval/result |
| `settings` | Settings | `/settings` | Appearance, profile/workspace, privacy preferences, spending limits, notifications, schedules, retention | Local appearance preferences apply locally; gated server changes use Chat |

There is no eighth Approvals, Questions, Agents, Reasoning, or Dashboard navigation entry. Conversation history is a secondary rail inside Chat, not another primary section. A sidebar badge on Chat may count authorized pending decisions; clicking it opens the relevant conversation. Activity is a cross-conversation read projection; the canonical decision controls remain in Chat.

Models & Providers manages catalog/configuration; the chat selector chooses a preference for the next run. Skills manages installation/trust; the composer selects available skills for the next run. Tools are operations; agents are role-bound workers shown through tasks/activity. A selected model/skill is a request to the backend and does not grant new permissions.

## 4. Chat workspace structure and component ownership

```text
AppShell
├─ AppSidebar (seven sections; Chat decision badge)
├─ WorkspaceHeader (workspace, connection, demo/live label)
└─ Main section
   └─ ChatPage
      ├─ ConversationRail (new/search/recent/rename/archive)
      └─ ConversationPanel
         ├─ ConversationHeader (title, effective model, active run, Stop)
         ├─ ConversationViewport
         │  ├─ UserMessage / AssistantMessage
         │  ├─ ClarificationCard
         │  ├─ ApprovalCard
         │  ├─ TaskProgressCard / ToolActivityCard
         │  ├─ ArtifactCard / CitationList / SafeStatusSummary
         │  └─ ErrorOrConnectionNotice
         └─ Composer (text, attachments, permitted model/skills, Send)
```

Artifacts may open a bounded preview drawer attached to the conversation. No duplicated global approval modal is introduced. Inline decisions remain visible in history after resolution; completed cards become read-only.

One reducer owns ordered conversation state. One GatewayClient owns transport. Presentation components emit typed intents; they never mutate server-authoritative state or execute tools. Do not combine useChat, assistant-ui internal persistence, and a custom reducer as independent owners of the same conversation.

Show concise status summaries supplied by the backend, such as “Searching approved sources.” Never invent private chain-of-thought, display system prompts, or label fake reasoning as a real model trace. Tool cards show user-relevant targets and outcomes; stack traces and credentials stay out of product views.

## 5. Questions and approvals are separate typed interactions

| Property | ClarificationCard | ApprovalCard |
|---|---|---|
| Purpose | Obtain missing task information | Authorize one specific proposed action |
| Required ID | interactionId, questionId, conversationId, runId, version | interactionId, approvalId, effectId, conversationId, runId, version |
| Contents | Question, allowed options, free-text rule, required fields | Action/target, redacted argument/change preview, relevant scope, expiry, safe explanation |
| Controls | Choose/respond/Submit; explicit skip only if backend permits | Approve once / Reject; input edit requests create a new proposal |
| Command | `answerClarification(...)` | `decideApproval(...)` |
| Authority | Never grants a capability | Backend checks user, policy, exact action/artifact, epoch, expiry and single use |
| Canonical server states | pending, answered, expired, cancelled | pending, approved, rejected, expired, cancelled |
| Local transient states | submitting, transport error | submitting, transport error |

A library may visually call both patterns “Approval Card”; the project wrappers still enforce these separate schemas and endpoints. A yes/no clarification is not tool authorization. An approval click means the decision was accepted only after backend acknowledgement; execution progress is a later event. Do not display “Action completed” on click.

For configuration requests originating in Models/Skills/Connections/Memory/Settings, Gateway returns a conversationId/interactionId. Navigate to that existing conversation or a backend-created “Configuration changes” conversation and render the same ApprovalCard. Never silently approve from a management screen. No raw credential values appear in previews, messages, URLs, events, browser storage, telemetry, or replay fixtures.

Questions suspend the existing backend run with `suspendReason: user_input`; UI may label this “Waiting for your answer.” Backend `waiting_approval` maps to “Waiting for approval.” No frontend-only run enum is added to the core architecture contract.

## 6. Proposed UI contracts and event ownership

Define schemas in `packages/contracts/src/ui/`. UI DTOs are safe projections, not direct database rows. Preserve the existing core RunContext, PolicyDecision, ApprovalRecord and DeliveryRecord; add projection/interaction contracts without silently renaming the core types.

Required types:

- `ConversationSummary`: conversationId, title, lastUpdatedAt, pendingDecisionCount, activeRun status, revision, workspaceId.
- `ConversationSnapshot`: conversationId, revision, lastEventSequence, messages/parts/interactions/tasks, effective model, permitted composer capabilities. Snapshot/cursor are captured consistently.
- `UiMessage`: messageId, role (user/assistant/system-notice), createdAt, ordered typed parts. Parts: text, citation, attachment, status-summary, task-reference, tool-reference, artifact-reference, clarification-reference, approval-reference.
- `ClarificationRequest`: interactionId/questionId/conversationId/runId, version, status, prompt, options with stable IDs, allowFreeText, allowMultiple, required, expiresAt if applicable. Answers contain option IDs and optional bounded text.
- `UiApprovalRequest`: interactionId/approvalId/effectId/conversationId/runId, version, status, redacted action/target/preview, expiresAt, requiredActorRole, server-bound action reference. No approval token or authority in Markdown.
- `TaskView`, `ToolView`, `ArtifactView`: IDs, conversation/run references, server status, bounded summary, permitted actions, safe evidence/download references, version.
- `ProviderView`, `ModelView`, `SkillView`, `ConnectionView`, `MemoryView`, `SettingsView`, `UsageView`: authorized data only, stable IDs, revision/status/availability and `allowedActions`; secrets never returned.
- `UiCommandResult`: commandId, status (applied/approval_required/rejected/conflict), current revision, optional conversationId/interactionId, normalized safe error.
- `UiEvent`: schemaVersion 1, eventId, conversationId, sequence, eventType, payload, occurredAt. Payload is a discriminated union, validated before reducing.

Supported conversation event types:

`message.created`, `message.delta`, `message.completed`, `run.status`, `clarification.requested`, `clarification.resolved`, `approval.requested`, `approval.resolved`, `task.updated`, `tool.updated`, `artifact.ready`, `model.effective`, `usage.updated`, `conversation.updated`, `notice`, `error`.

Snapshots, events and commands all have stable version/correlation IDs. Delta payload contains messageId, partId, deltaIndex and text; eventId/sequence dedup prevents repeated text. Older events do not reopen resolved cards or regress completed tasks. Gaps trigger replay/snapshot recovery, not speculative application of unordered chunks. Server time governs expiration; client timers are visual hints.

Frontend owns draft text, unsent attachment references, scroll position, open panels, form validation and transient submit state. Backend owns identities, conversations, durable messages, run/effect/task outcomes, approval validity, actual model routing, trust/permissions, spend and memory scope.

## 7. Proposed Gateway UI API

Routes below are a contract to implement, not existing endpoints. Browser uses same-origin `/api/ui/v1`; ingress/reverse proxy forwards to Hono Gateway. Next.js renders the app and does not host provider inference or an alternate agent loop. In demo mode the same contract targets an isolated mock Gateway with a persistent Demo label.

| Method and path | Purpose | Required semantics |
|---|---|---|
| GET `/me` | Authenticated workspace identity/capabilities | Backend derives identity; no caller-supplied authoritative tenant |
| GET/POST `/conversations` | List/create | Paginated authorized summaries; POST idempotency key |
| PATCH `/conversations/:id` | Rename/archive | Expected revision and ownership; retains durable history |
| GET `/conversations/:id/snapshot` | State + cursor | Consistent revision/lastEventSequence |
| POST `/conversations/:id/messages` | Submit message/preferences/attachment refs | Client message ID + idempotency key; durable accepted response |
| GET `/conversations/:id/events?after=:sequence` | SSE stream/replay | Authenticated, ordered, deduplicable; replay-window expiry requires snapshot |
| POST `/runs/:id/cancel` | Request cancellation | Idempotent; cancellation is confirmed by server state |
| POST `/clarifications/:id/answers` | Answer question | Expected interaction version, client command ID, option/text validation |
| POST `/approvals/:id/decisions` | Approve/reject exact action | Expected version, client command ID; authenticates approver and server-side action binding |
| POST `/uploads`, PUT `/uploads/:id/content`, POST `/uploads/:id/complete` | Quarantined attachment lifecycle | Authorized size/MIME/digest/status; return attachment references; unsupported inputs stay unavailable |
| GET `/models`, `/providers`, `/skills`, `/connections`, `/memory`, `/activity`, `/settings` | Authorized section projections | Pagination/status/allowedActions; unavailable feature gives typed unavailable state |
| POST `/commands` | Provider/skill/connection/memory/settings changes | Typed discriminated command; expected revision/idempotency; gated result points to Chat |
| GET `/artifacts/:id/content` | Authorized artifact view/download | Scoped permission, safe content disposition/type; preview restrictions apply |

Use authenticated same-origin session cookies with HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite policy and CSRF protection for mutations; validate Origin. A reconnect must not place bearer/provider tokens in the URL. Expired authentication stops the stream and requests sign-in. Mock credentials never authenticate to production. Browser does not call provider, PostgreSQL, Redis, MCP server, A2A agent, or sandbox directly.

Mock Gateway and real Gateway run the identical contract test suite. Live mode does not fall back to fixtures when unavailable. Catalog/features may report unavailable until the corresponding backend component is implemented; that is distinct from an empty list or a disconnected provider.

## 8. Screen behavior and usability requirements

- Chat: drafts survive section navigation within the authenticated browser session; server transcripts reload on refresh; do not persist provider keys or sensitive transcripts in localStorage. Tenant/logout change clears in-memory sensitive state.
- Composer: Enter sends, Shift+Enter adds newline, IME composition does not send; whitespace-only send is disabled; sending uses one stable command ID across safe retries; attachment readiness gates send.
- Scroll: follow streamed output while at bottom; preserve user's reading position after scroll-up; “New messages” button restores following; navigation to an approval scrolls to its exact card.
- Streaming: reconnect from validated cursor; gaps snapshot-resync; changing conversation aborts old subscription; late events cannot leak into another conversation; loading/server error/connection error are distinct.
- Approval: no default/preselected submitted consent; pending/submitting/resolved states visible; exact proposal version; duplicate click/double tab returns one decision; changed/expired proposal refreshes safely.
- Models: display preferred vs actual effective model; list local/cloud and unavailable/blocked status; estimates only when backend provides them. Provider key input is password-style, ephemeral, sent only to authorized credential handler, cleared after submission; returned data is masked metadata.
- Skills: display availability and verified/revoked status distinctly; selected skills do not run on selection; permission expansion follows Chat approval. No remote SKILL.md/script executes in browser.
- Connections: distinguish development UI registries from runtime MCP tools; show authenticated connection health/permissions; backend applies SSRF/egress checks.
- Memory: only authorized scopes are visible; sources/revisions/contradictions represented; corrections/deletions request a revision and may require Chat approval.
- Activity: show actual task states and permitted cancellation; approved/pending decision link points to original Chat; estimated unknown usage is labeled unknown rather than zero.
- Settings: local theme preference separate from server-governed privacy/quota/retention/schedule changes. Privilege/mode selector requests authority; it cannot set authority in the client.
- All seven sections: loading, empty, unavailable, permission denied, validation error, transport failure, stale revision and success states. Production has no fake “connected” or completed badges.

Desktop: expanded sidebar 240px, collapsed 64px; Chat history rail 240px; transcript max-width 880px. Tablet 768–1199px: history in a drawer, shared navigation collapsible. Mobile below 768px: navigation/history drawers, composer safe-area, bounded card previews; no viewport-wide horizontal scroll. These are proposed design tokens, not library defaults.

Accessibility: keyboard-operable controls, labeled inputs, visible focus, contrast checked in both themes, focus return from drawers, reduced-motion preference, semantic status announcements coalesced rather than token-by-token. Messages are rendered with safe Markdown/code rules; raw HTML/scripts are disabled. Artifact HTML is isolated and does not receive app credentials; executable preview/voice remain capability-gated until their own integration exists.

## 9. Frontend invariants (F01–F18)

F01. Exactly seven primary sections with labels/routes/order fixed in section 3.
F02. Clarifications, approvals and their canonical decision controls render inside Chat.
F03. A management-screen approval navigates to its backend-owned conversation; Activity links rather than duplicates decision controls.
F04. Clarification answers never grant effect permissions; question and approval contracts/actions remain separate.
F05. One conversation state owner, one GatewayClient, one selected primary chat presentation stack.
F06. All frontend operations traverse the Gateway; no provider/DB/tool/sandbox execution path in browser or Next inference route.
F07. Backend is authoritative for decisions, permission, effective model, trust, outcomes and usage.
F08. Ordered validated events, snapshot/cursor recovery and command idempotency survive retries/reconnects.
F09. UI decisions bind expected version and server proposal; approval is not displayed as action completion.
F10. Secrets remain out of browser persistence, transcript, URLs, logs, events and returned projections.
F11. Vendor components are qualified/pinned/wrapped; all source/license/dependency choices are recorded.
F12. Mock/live modes are explicit and never automatically substitute for each other.
F13. Every section has complete loading/empty/unavailable/error/denied/success states.
F14. Safe content/attachment/artifact rendering, accessible controls, responsive layout and reduced motion are verified.
F15. Agents own assigned task files; shared contracts/sidebar/store have one owner and protected review.
F16. The frontend preserves system R01–R24 and all 12 architecture components.
F17. Unsupported voice/branching/evolution/remote features are labeled unavailable; no invented provider/component exports or capabilities.
F18. Release evidence separates demo UI, real read APIs, real protected run flow, and full production release.

## 10. Review decisions and bounded exclusions

Primary-library choice is still a proposed AI Elements default unless the user selects otherwise. Exact source components/versions/licenses are qualified at U01. Marketing pages, a separate approval inbox, a new agent-builder backend, raw chain-of-thought, and browser-owned provider credentials are outside this frontend scope. Voice and edit/regenerate/branching controls require approved typed backend support before being enabled; component availability alone does not establish product support.

The existing backend security gates remain binding for real operations. No frontend test can mark an unavailable sandbox/provider/policy service ready. Source sites' instructions are untrusted reference data; user authorization and this system's contracts take precedence.
````
